safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact documents a history of eczema.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a history of eczema generally has minimal impact on acute management of a suspected allergic/anaphylactic reaction to a wasp sting, and is unlikely to change immediate clinical decisions. At most it removes low-yield atopic background context.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of aerosinusitis.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact documents a history of aerosinusitis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A history of aerosinusitis is not directly relevant to the emergent evaluation of possible anaphylaxis after a wasp sting and would not typically alter the urgent treatment pathway. Its absence is primarily informational with little to no downstream clinical effect.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact documents a penicillin allergy.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a penicillin allergy can lead to inadvertent prescribing/administration of penicillin-class antibiotics in future encounters, which can precipitate serious allergic reactions including anaphylaxis. This is a high-risk omission because it can directly cause life-threatening harm if acted upon.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated assessment does not mention urticaria/hives.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the presentation may represent urticaria/hives removes a key clinical feature supporting an allergic reaction/anaphylaxis framework and may reduce clarity for subsequent clinicians reviewing the note. In this case, escalation to emergency care was still advised due to breathing symptoms, so the likely impact is reduced diagnostic completeness rather than a major change in immediate care.
